title_en: Those they invoke cannot create a fly
notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The ayah addresses people: a similitude is struck, so listen to it: those you call upon besides God will never create a fly, even if they gathered for it.
If the fly takes something from them, they cannot rescue it from it; weak are the seeker and the sought.
They did not appraise God with His true appraisal; God is strong and mighty.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah addresses people with a similitude: those they call upon besides God will never create a fly, even if they gathered for it [c1]. If the fly takes something from them, they cannot rescue it from it [c2].
chapters.body_md:
The ayah addresses people: a similitude is struck, so listen to it [c1]. Those you call upon besides God will never create a fly, even if they gathered for it [c1]. If the fly takes something from them, they cannot rescue it from it [c2]. The ayah says that the seeker and the sought are weak [c2].

The next ayah says that they did not appraise God with His true appraisal [c3]. It adds that God is strong and mighty [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The similitude is introduced as something to be listened to, and its content is statements about those who are called upon besides God [c1][c2]. The words weak are the seeker and the sought close the picture, and the next ayah turns to how God was appraised [c2][c3]. The ayah does not say which one is the seeker and which the sought [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The ayah says that those people call upon besides God will never create a fly, even if they gathered for it [c1]. If the fly takes something from them, they cannot rescue it [c2]. God is strong and mighty [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture sets the creation of a fly beside those who are called upon besides God [c1]. Another reading is that the next ayah closes by saying that they did not appraise God with His true appraisal and that God is strong and mighty [c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who those called upon besides God are; the ayah names none.
- Not established: what was taken by the fly or who held it; the ayah says something and does not name it.
- The words the seeker and the sought (al-talib wa-l-matlub) are read in more than one way, since the ayah does not say which is the fly and which the one called upon.
- The ayah itself says that a similitude is struck (duriba mathal).

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to these ayat.
Who the seeker and the sought are is for a scholar to decide.
